notice: Hands-on labs, defined day by day. Every lab is LAB / TEST ENVIRONMENT only: fictional data or isolated test systems, never production.

labs.title: Build a risk register for a fictional bank
labs.environment: LAB / TEST ENVIRONMENT: a new spreadsheet with fictional data only. Do not use real company risks, systems or names.
labs.goal: Turn a scenario into a working risk register with owners, ratings, treatments and an acceptance decision, and do one quantitative calculation.
prerequisites: A spreadsheet app (Excel, LibreOffice or Google Sheets)
Read the Mukuvisi Bank case study in Questions → Scenario sets
Cards: risk treatment, SLE/ARO/ALE, control types
steps: Create columns: ID, risk statement (threat + vulnerability + asset), owner, likelihood (1-5), impact (1-5), inherent score, existing controls, treatment, residual likelihood, residual impact, residual score, acceptance authority, review date.
Write five risks for the fictional Mukuvisi Bank, for example ransomware on core banking, stale policy, unclassified data, single telecom carrier, insider fraud in payments.
Score likelihood and impact for each and compute inherent score = likelihood × impact.
Choose a treatment for each (avoid, mitigate, transfer, accept) and name one control per mitigated risk, labelled by type (preventive, detective, corrective, deterrent, compensating).
Re-score residual likelihood and impact after treatment and compute the residual score.
Set an appetite rule, for example residual 1-6 accepted by department head, 8-12 by executive, 15+ by board, and fill in the acceptance authority column.
For the ransomware risk, estimate asset value, exposure factor and annual rate of occurrence; compute SLE and ALE in a separate cell and compare with the annual cost of one control.
validation: Every risk names an owner from the business, not only IT.
Every risk has a treatment, a residual score and a review date.
Acceptance authority rises with residual score as your appetite rule says.
SLE = asset value × exposure factor and ALE = SLE × ARO are calculated correctly.
rollback: Nothing to roll back: the lab touches no system. Delete the spreadsheet if you do not want to keep it.
evidence: Export the register as PDF or a screenshot.
A three-sentence summary for the fictional board: top risk, recommended treatment, decision needed.

labs.title: Run a mini business impact analysis on a test service
labs.environment: LAB / TEST ENVIRONMENT: a fictional service or one you run in an isolated home or test lab. Do not interview colleagues or use production systems.
labs.goal: Practise turning business impact into MTD, RTO and RPO, and surface dependencies, before any recovery design.
prerequisites: Pick one fictional business process, for example 'agent cash-in for a mobile money service'
Cards: RTO, RPO, WRT, MTD; drill: RTO, RPO, MTD and WRT
steps: Describe the process in two sentences and name its owner.
List what it depends on: systems, data, people, suppliers, utilities, telecom links.
Estimate the impact of an outage at 1 hour, 4 hours, 1 day and 3 days: money, regulatory, reputation, safety.
Mark the point where impact becomes unacceptable: that is the MTD.
Estimate the work recovery time after a restore (checks, reconciliation) and set RTO = MTD − WRT or lower.
Set the RPO from how much data the process can lose and still be reconstructed.
Mark every single point of failure in the dependency list.
validation: RTO + WRT does not exceed MTD.
At least one external dependency is listed.
No recovery solution or vendor appears in the output: the BIA states requirements only.
rollback: Nothing to roll back: this is a paper exercise.
evidence: The completed impact table and the MTD, RTO, RPO line.
The list of single points of failure, ranked.
